I've been growing cotton in Quzhou my whole farming life. Thirty years on this same flat land in southern Hebei — I know what it wants. My kids take factory work to supplement income, but the farm runs on cotton. All 13.1 mu of it. That won't change this year.

I'll plant in late April after the soil warms past the last frost risk. I switched to Bt hybrid seed years ago — it cut the bollworm work dramatically and my neighbors who still use traditional seed spend weeks more on spraying. I plough every spring, work in base fertilizer at the same time. I don't do no-tillage; this soil needs breaking up after winter.

Fertilizer — I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then top-dress with urea twice during boll setting. That's where the yield is built. I've settled on roughly 16 kg of nitrogen per mu over the years. Less and the bolls are small. More and I get too much vegetative growth and waste money.

Irrigation — I run the well 5 times: once to establish seedlings, once at budding, twice during peak flowering and boll set, and once more if August stays dry. That's been my pattern for years and it works.

Pesticides — even with the Bt cotton I still spray 8 times through the season. Aphids in early summer, mites in July, fungal disease if it's humid. I can't afford to lose bolls to something I could have controlled.

I expect 300 kg/mu of seed cotton if nothing goes badly wrong. Some years 280, some years 320. That's my life.
